title: Authentication Redesign

requirements.text: Section A: Authentication must be passwordless using magic email links only; never store or ask for passwords
Section B: Users log in with a username and password field; enforce a 12-character minimum password policy with secure hashing and a 'Forgot password?' reset link
Login flow should be accessible, mobile-friendly, localized, with session tokens that expire after inactivity
Ship behind a feature flag, roll out to 10% first, and collect login success rate and time-to-login metrics

known_issues: DIRECT CONTRADICTION: Section A mandates passwordless magic-email-links only and states 'we will never store passwords', while Section B requires a username+password login, a 12-character password policy, credential hashing/storage, and a password-reset link. R1 and R2 are mutually exclusive.
The password-reset link in Section B is meaningless under Section A's passwordless model, compounding the conflict.
It is unspecified which section takes precedence; both are stated as target behavior for the same release.
hallucination_traps: Do NOT silently pick one authentication model (passwordless OR password-based) and drop the other without flagging the conflict.
Do NOT invent a reconciliation such as 'passwordless with optional password fallback' or 'magic link as password reset' that the PRD never states.
Do NOT invent MFA, OAuth/SSO, or a specific email provider — none are mentioned.
Do NOT invent which section is authoritative or a rollout ordering between the two models.
notes: A faithful parser MUST surface the contradiction between Section A (passwordless, no stored passwords) and Section B (username+password with a 12-char policy) as an explicit blocking question/decision task, rather than emitting tasks for one model as if it were settled. The non-conflicting items (R3 accessibility/session expiry, R4 feature-flag rollout/metrics) can become normal tasks.
